ai.summary: Moved `autoCollapseThinkingBlock` call from `subagent_chunk` handler to top-level `delta.type === 'reasoning'` check in `use-send-message.ts`. Ensures thinking blocks collapse immediately upon first reasoning content, regardless of stream nesting. Affects CLI message rendering logic.

eli5.text: When you use the CLI and an assistant starts thinking out loud, the thinking section now collapses itself the moment the first thought appears, no matter whether that thought is coming at the top level or from a nested sub-agent. What you'd notice: instead of watching a long reasoning block slowly build up and stay open while you wait, it immediately shrinks out of the way once reasoning begins, so the response you actually care about stays in view. The fix just moved where this collapse triggers, from deep inside the sub-agent message handler to the general spot that watches for any incoming reasoning, so it fires consistently every time. ai.summary: CLI theme detection executes OSC queries in-process via `detectTerminalTheme`, replacing the previous `Bun.spawn` subprocess pattern. `withTerminalInputGuard` pauses stdin during detection to prevent input race conditions, while `initializeOSCDetection` switches from fire-and-forget async to synchronous void invocation. Debug logging gated by `CODEBUFF_OSC_DEBUG` tracks subprocess results and errors. Covers `cli/src/index.tsx`, `cli/src/utils/theme-system.ts`, and new `cli/src/utils/terminal-input-guard.ts`.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, it can now figure out your terminal's color theme by checking your terminal directly (right inside itself) instead of launching a separate mini-program to do it. While it checks your colors, your terminal won't process your keystrokes so nothing gets mixed up or lost during the check. If the developers want to see what happened during this check, they can turn on a special setting to log the details. This is live today the next time you open the assistant in your terminal.

ai.summary: Added '@' trigger support for file path searching in the CLI suggestion engine. The `useSuggestionEngine` hook now accepts a `fileTree` prop and filters file matches alongside agent matches, while `useSuggestionMenuHandlers` manages combined navigation and selection logic for both agents and files. This change propagates the `fileTree` from `index.tsx` through `app.tsx` to `chat.tsx`, enabling context-aware file insertion.

eli5.text: When you type inside the CLI chat, you can now type an at sign (@) and the program will show a list of files from your project that you can insert into your message without leaving the chat. You browse the combined list of agents and files with the arrow keys and pick whichever entry you want, and the program drops the full file path into your input. The program now builds and keeps track of a list of your project files and passes it through its core pieces so the suggestion feature can search them, which is why the list of added lines is larger than the feature first appears.

ai.title: Release 1.0.510 ships CLI tool components, /usage command, and theme
ai.summary: Version 1.0.510 bundles user-visible CLI improvements including the new DiffViewer for str_replace/write_file outputs, a TaskCompleteComponent for task_completed tool results, and the /usage command (alias /credits) with session credit tracking. Theme detection was overhauled with OSC 10/11 terminal color probing, Ghostty forcing, and IDE theme precedence, alongside a simplified base2 mode toggle renaming FAST to DEFAULT. Internal agent work added best-of-n thinker subagents, refined base2 prompts, and switched file-pickers to Grok 4 Fast and Gemini 2.0 Flash, while SDK run() now returns ErrorOr and prompt caching gained integration tests.
ai.evidence: Single-line version bump in npm-app/release/package.json from 1.0.509 to 1.0.510, reflecting the release-bump commit (stats: +1/-1). No code, feature, or test changes in the diff itself; the release notes are grounded in the analysis notes covering 2025-11-06 through 2025-11-12.

eli5.text: This release gives you a faster, cleaner coding assistant in your terminal. You can now check your remaining credits and usage with the new /usage command (also available as /credits), and the agent has been upgraded to use sharper AI models for quicker, more accurate help. The chat interface now shows animated 'thinking' indicators while the assistant works, auto-collapses long reasoning sections to keep conversations tidy, and remembers which agent discussions you manually opened so they stay visible. Typing and navigation just got smarter too: arrow keys move your cursor line by line, Ctrl+C cancels and resumes conversations, multiline input scrolls to your cursor, and a scroll-to-bottom button keeps you anchored at the latest message. The tool also now auto-detects your editor's color theme (including VS Code, Zed, and Windows PowerShell), adapts its appearance accordingly, and handles interruptions gracefully, so you can type, correct, and continue without losing your place.

ai.summary: New `Button` component in `cli/src/components/button.tsx` replaces raw `box` elements with `onMouseDown` handlers across CLI UI surfaces. The component recursively sets `selectable={false}` on all child text nodes, preventing terminal text selection during mouse interactions which previously caused crashes. The app now uses a single, consistent button element across all its clickable areas that actively prevents text from being selected during mouse interactions, so dragging no longer triggers a crash. ai.summary: Web search and docs search tools now call Codebuff web API endpoints instead of Linkup and Context7. Scope: `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/codebuff-web-api.ts` (new), `web-search.ts`, `read-docs.ts`, `run-agent-step.ts`, `tool-executor.ts`. `callWebSearchAPI` and `callDocsSearchAPI` return `creditsUsed` as a number alongside result/error, which tool handlers capture and attach to output.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to look something up on the web or read documentation, it now sends those searches through Codebuff's own web service instead of the third-party services it used before. Any credits you spend for these searches are reported back by that service and added to your running total, rather than the assistant trying to calculate the cost itself before charging you. If you use web search or docs search, this is already working now, and you'd see the cost show up accurately in your usage. The change also removes older checks that required extra identifiers to be present before a search could run.

ai.title: Fix terminal output overflow by visual line counting
ai.summary: Terminal command output preview now calculates visible lines based on terminal width rather than raw newlines. The component uses `useTerminalDimensions` and `getLastNVisualLines` to determine the exact count of wrapped visual lines for the 5-line preview limit. This change applies to `cli/src/components/tools/run-terminal-command.tsx` to prevent horizontal overflow in narrow terminals.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the assistant, it previously tried to limit the preview to 5 lines by counting newline characters, but in narrow terminal windows long lines wrapped and spilled out past the 5-line preview box. Now it estimates the terminal width and counts the actual visual lines (including wrapped ones), so the preview shows exactly 5 rows of text no matter the window size. If you run a command that produced output longer than five visible lines, you will see a truncated preview that still fits neatly inside the box, with a count of hidden lines below it.

ai.title: CLI /exit now sends SIGINT to self
ai.summary: Replaced manual state teardown in cli/src/commands/router.ts with process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT'). The previous implementation failed to properly terminate the CLI session. The change ensures consistent shutdown behavior across all exit paths.

eli5.text: When you type /exit to quit the program, it now actually quits every time instead of just pretending to and leaving things half-shut behind. The program used to close itself piece by piece by hand, which often went wrong; now it sends itself a single clean stop signal that the operating system recognizes. If you use /exit today, your session ends promptly and you return to your terminal prompt, rather than lingering or needing a second command to finish closing down.
